requirement:
In a book chapter, each valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference, inline
or fenced, renders as a Shields.io static badge image, subject to the
citation-only paragraph exception below and the reviewed-passage display under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review.book_commentary.display`.
The badge has meaningful alt text displaying its role and full name, and links
to the badge at the corresponding `{req}` or `{example}` definition. Links
work across chapters, including nested chapters. Apart from the reviewed-passage
exception, a fenced reference renders its badge followed by its body as Markdown.

Inside any prose-bearing colon-fenced section, top-level paragraphs containing
one or more valid inline `{cite}` references and otherwise only whitespace are
omitted from the chapter. This applies to requirements, examples, definitions,
reference fences, and other prose containers, including nested sections.
Requirement and example detail pages still render those citations.
Citations within explanatory prose, lists or blockquotes, unfenced chapter
prose, and references of other roles retain their usual rendering.
Escaped roles, code, raw HTML, and unresolvable references remain literal.
The original declaration, reference discovery, and authoring inputs retain the
citations.

Each fenced `{req}` or `{example}` directive renders with a badge identifying
its kind and full name; text outside a directive remains literal. Declaration
badge navigation follows {cite}`requirements.index.navigation`.
Badge text remains legible regardless of whether its link has been visited.
A badge link shows a visible indicator when it has keyboard focus and may
brighten on hover. Badges may be laid out inline with the surrounding text, a
fenced reference's badge and body may be visually set apart from the surrounding
text as one block, and a built-in's unlinked badge may show a help cursor to
signal its hover text. These badges use the syntax defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`.
rationale: structural: Every clause of `requirements.references.book_badges` describes observable rendered output, so I found no structural obligation that needs implementation evidence. I checked each candidate clause for an alternative implementation that keeps the same output but breaks the clause: - "renders as a Shields.io static badge image", with alt text showing role and full name, and links to the `{req}` or `{example}` definition. This fixes the output form: a Shields.io image, its alt text and its link target. It names no function, type, signature, library or delegation. The current `src/lib.rs#fn[shield_badge]` builds the `img.shields.io` URL and `` tag. A differently factored generator, such as inline formatting or another helper, would give the same book output and still satisfy the text. Which function builds the badge is discretionary. - Links work across chapters, fenced references render the badge followed by the body, and citation-only paragraphs are omitted. These are output and filtering behaviors. How they are coded is not prescribed. - "Badge text remains legible regardless of whether its link has been visited", a visible keyboard-focus indicator, optional hover brightening, optional inline layout, and a help cursor for built-ins. These are visual behaviors. `md/habeas.css` has matching rules, including `rule[a.habeas-req-badge,%20a.habeas-req-badge:visited]` and `rule[a.habeas-req-badge:focus-visible]`. Another stylesheet or inline styles could give the same display, so the CSS file is not structurally mandated. The text also says several of these are optional ("may"). - The declaration badge navigation and the badge syntax are delegated by `{cite}` to `requirements.index.navigation` and `requirements.references.roles`. Those are context, not obligations of this requirement. Because only observable behavior is specified, the supplied roots (`src/lib.rs#fn[shield_badge]` and `md/habeas.css`) are acceptable but not required. No missing root is reported. Tests for the rendering behavior belong to the behavioral criterion. behavioral: I judged the tests adequate for each observable obligation in `requirements.references.book_badges`. I did not read implementation source, and I did not assess the cited requirements' own tests. - **Inline badges, alt text, links, nested chapters:** `references_in_nested_chapters_link_to_the_requirement_definition` renders inline `{impl}`, `{cite}` and `{test}` references from `guides/deep.md`. It asserts the Shields image URL for each role, the role-specific class, and the `../requirements.html#habeas-req-...` link. `shields_badge_urls_escape_requirement_names` asserts the badge URL and the `alt="req "` text. `examples_are_distinct_definitions_and_tests_link_to_them` checks a `{test}` link to an `{example}` from a nested chapter. - **Fenced references:** `fenced_references_render_their_badge_and_body_and_built_ins_are_unlinked` covers all three roles. For each it asserts the linked badge with `alt=" rules.other"` and the Shields URL. It also asserts that the Markdown-rendered body (``) follows the badge and that the raw fence text is gone. - **Built-in badges:** the same test checks that built-in badges are unlinked and carry hover text, both inline and fenced. - **Literal cases:** - `fenced_references_render_their_badge_and_body_and_built_ins_are_unlinked` covers unresolvable and invalid names (`rules.missing`, `habeas:none`) and a fence inside a code block. - `markdown_examples_and_escaped_references_stay_literal` covers escaped roles and code spans. - `roles_in_raw_html_stay_literal` covers raw HTML. - `colon_directives_render_markdown_bodies_and_legacy_roles_stay_literal` covers an inline `{req}` role. - **Citation-only paragraph omission:** - `citation_metadata_is_hidden_in_fenced_sections_and_preserved_in_details` runs the omission over req, example, definition, note, and the cite, impl and test reference fences. It asserts the omission from the chapter, the preservation on the detail page, and that the source file, definitions and authoring inputs are unchanged. - `citation_metadata_preserves_prose_other_roles_and_literal_contexts` covers the exceptions: explanatory prose, lists, blockquotes, other roles, code, raw HTML, invalid or unknown citations, and unclosed or unfenced sections. It also covers nested sections and CRLF line endings. - **Req and example declaration badges:** `colon_directives_render_markdown_bodies_and_legacy_roles_stay_literal` checks the declaration `id`, the Markdown body, and that the surrounding text stays literal. `fenced_references_render_their_badge_and_body_and_built_ins_are_unlinked` and `examples_are_distinct_definitions_and_tests_link_to_them` check the `aria-label` identifying kind and full name. Navigation behaviour belongs to the cited `requirements.index.navigation`, and the tests that carry `{test}` markers for it also cover the badge name links. - **Styling:** `badge_stylesheet_keeps_visited_links_legible_and_shows_focus` asserts that visited rules match unvisited ones, that the focus-visible outline is visible, and that hover only brightens. The hover and help-cursor allowances are MAY clauses and need no test. The reviewed-passage display is delegated to `requirements.references.citation_review.book_commentary.display`, and I did not assess it here. I found no unmarked relevant tests and no uncovered MUST or SHOULD clause.

:::{req} citation_review.book_commentary.display
In authored book chapters, a passage opted into citation review under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review.book_commentary` displays its
body as ordinary Markdown prose, with the same left alignment as the
surrounding prose and no opening citation badge or enclosing border.
A small marker in the right gutter identifies the passage's citation-checking
annotations. It does not claim that recorded evidence is current or accepted.
The outermost eligible citation fence has one marker; nested commentary
belongs to its list rather than displaying another marker.
Activating the marker opens the list of resolved citations from the source
passage, including its opening citation, citation-only metadata paragraphs,
and citations within nested commentary. Citations belonging to nested
requirement or example declarations are excluded. Repeated citations appear
once. Project citations link to their declarations; built-in citations retain
their descriptive hover text. The marker is keyboard operable, has an
accessible label, and shows visible keyboard focus. Opening the list does not
hide the passage. Inline citations within explanatory prose retain their
usual rendering.
Rendering does not change the source passage, its discovered references, or
its review inputs. Unfenced citations, citations inside requirement or example
declarations, and utility-only commentary retain their existing rendering.
:::{req} navigation
Each requirement and example declaration badge has two adjacent links. Its
kind (`req` or `example`) links to the declaration's anchor on the current
page; its full name links to the evidence detail page. These segments stay
together in one non-wrapping row, with no separate arrow link or plaintext evidence link.
Each detail page links back to the declaration's anchored badge and to the
index. Reference badges continue to link to the declaration. These links
resolve when a requirement name contains `.md`, as in
`requirements.cli.mdbook`.
:::{req} roles

Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name, or with a built-in name under {cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, and MAY use the `{fixme}` role in fenced form. A reference MAY instead be written in fenced form, `:::{role} name` on one line, a body, and a closing fence, following the fence rules of {cite}`requirements.ci.span` and {cite}`requirements.ci.fence_lengths`; the fenced form is the same edge with attached commentary, and the inline form carries none. In a source comment, fence lines MUST be recognized after removing each line's comment delimiters within one comment run under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`, and a fence that does not close within its comment run MUST be a validation error. Each reference is a directed edge between its source and the named definition. A source is a {term}`requirements.references.source_item` or a requirement or example declaration. The roles MUST mean:
- `{cite}`: the source relies on, supports, or refers to the definition. It is an
edge from the source to the definition.
- `{impl}`: the source implements part of the definition: it makes a decision,
performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case that the definition
specifies. A requirement MAY implement part of another requirement by refining
one of its obligations. Calling code that implements a definition, or
producing a result a caller uses to meet it, MUST NOT by itself count as
implementing it. A check MUST count only if the definition states it, or the
source could not meet one of the definition's obligations without it; source
that checks it is consistent with a definition, such as recognizing a form the
definition specifies in order to decide whether to run other behavior, relies
on that definition and calls for `{cite}`. A requirement stating a convention
for every output of a kind, such as every validation error, is implemented by
the source that carries out the convention as a whole, such as the step that
collects and reports those outputs.
- `{test}`: the source is designed to verify behavior the definition specifies:
a test through its scenario and the assertions about that scenario's outcome,
or a named example through the concrete case it describes.
- `{fixme}`: the source acknowledges a known gap in fulfilling the definition. It
MUST use the fenced form, and its body MUST describe the gap. The body MAY
begin with option lines naming issues that track the gap, one per line, in the
form `:github: <owner>/<repo>#<number>`, such as
`:github: rust-lang/rust#123`. `github` MUST be the only recognized option.
A named `{fixme}` MAY appear only in sources outside the book. Validation MUST report
any other option line, a `:github:` value not in that form, an inline
`{fixme}`, a `{fixme}` in a requirement or example declaration, and a
`{fixme}` whose body, without option lines and comment delimiters, is empty.
An unnamed `{fixme}`, a fence of `:::{fixme}` with no name, MAY appear in any
project text, including a requirement or example body, to tie that place to
the issues it names. It MUST have at least one `:github:` option line and MAY
have a description; it is not a reference edge, acknowledges no gap, and needs
no evidence input. Its issues are checked under {cite}`requirements.cli.fixme_issues`.
`{impl}`, `{test}`, and `{fixme}` are edges from the definition to the source.
Code implementations are reviewed as part of the definitions they implement or
test. Citation reviews assess cited source items and book passages under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
```text
{impl}`requirements.references.roles`
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`
{test}`requirements.references.roles`
:::{definition} source_item
:phrase: source item
A node in a project file’s outline, identified by the project-relative path
and an outline selector. For example, `src/auth.rs#fn[check_token]` identifies
a Rust function. The root node represents the whole file. A reference in a
comment belongs to the item that owns the comment under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
